verifiable-quality-gates.why: the fix is a .gitattributes rule whose effect (every text file checks out LF) must be proven, not asserted, with a test that fails if the rule is dropped.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added test/line-endings.test.mjs that asks git check-attr eol for representative skill/doc/json/script files and asserts each resolves to lf; dropping eol=lf makes git report unspecified and fails it.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: a deliberate repo-wide line-ending policy decision with non-obvious mechanics (blobs already LF; only checkout changes) and honest limits.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0090 (force eol=lf repo-wide so skills check out LF on Windows; no content rewrite; renormalize note for existing-CRLF consumers).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the change is a .mjs test enumerating the checkout-attribute behavior by file type (a changed .mjs is a behavior surface).
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases asserting git resolves eol=lf for a SKILL.md, two scripts, a JSON, a top-level doc, and the directive.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the risk is git's checkout attribute resolution; the test exercises it via git check-attr at the layer that owns it.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: an integration test that runs git check-attr against the real committed/working .gitattributes for representative files.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR claims no content rewrite and names what the fix does not reach; those claims need an evidence state and a named limitation.
skeptical-audit.what: stated the honest limits in ADR-0090 (blobs already LF so nothing is rewritten; a consumer with existing CRLF commits renormalizes once; applies to clones honoring the attribute) and verified the index is all i/lf.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a repo-wide attribute change (which could accidentally ship a mass content diff or affect binaries) must pass the four-questions review before done.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context subagent review of the staged diff (confirming it is config+test+docs only, not a 322-file renormalization, and binary-safe); recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, secret, or file-handling control; a line-ending checkout attribute.

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern; a one-line .gitattributes rule.

arch-encode.why: no new recurring rule file; the behavior is pinned by its own discrimination test.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, migration, retention, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system/data architecture or service-boundary change; repo line-ending config.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy mechanics, migration, flag, or rollback change.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.
